title: Model Scout Mosaic & Customer Funnel Mapping
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Run a targeted competitive and customer-facing scan that links model capability mosaics to buyer funnel behaviors for mid-market and enterprise customers. The goal is to produce an operational playbook that: (1) prioritizes candidate open models and variants by commercial fit, latency/econ trade-offs, and upgrade path; (2) maps model capability gaps to concrete buyer-funnel stages (discovery, POC, pilot, procurement, renewal); and (3) produces sentinel triggers and a weekly scouting cadence for new entrants or capability shifts.
objectives: Create a 'mosaic' taxonomy that combines model capabilities (generation, instruction-following, embeddings fidelity, RAG compatibility, safety heuristics) with deployment economics (quantization delta, throughput, region availability).
Map the mosaic results to customer funnel stages and define intervention playbooks for Product, Solutions, and Sales.
Ship a lightweight dashboard (spreadsheet + confluence doc) and a weekly scout digest with signal severity scoring and recommended actions.
acceptance_criteria: Mosaic taxonomy published in Confluence with at least 12 representative model entries from different providers and quant/precision variants.
Customer-funnel mapping that prescribes 3 tactical interventions per funnel stage (e.g., RAG fallback policy for POC, latency SLAs for pilot).
Weekly scout digest template implemented and automated to pull four telemetry sources (public release notes, model hub changelogs, benchmark lab, sales field reports).
Hand-off package for Solutions team: one-pager, playbook checklist, and two exemplar prompt suites for regression checks.
research_findings: Preliminary lab runs show that mid-market RAG workloads are highly sensitive to 50–100ms p95 token-latency shifts; embedding switch tests reveal semantic drift >6% in recall for domain-specific corpora when switching quantized variants. Sales win/loss notes indicate that procurement asks for predictable upgrade paths and documented fallback contracts. Open-source entrants tend to ship capability changes (instruction tuning, longer context) without clear backward compatibility guarantees—this drives a need for 'compatibility hedges' in our playbook.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Trade-off: maintaining broad model coverage vs. depth of vetting. Decided to prioritize depth for 3 target verticals (finserv, documentation tooling, CRM automation) and keep a lightweight watchlist for the rest. We will accept a small increase in initial integration effort to reduce downstream outage risk. Recommended policy: only promote model variants to 'fallback-ready' after a 2-week smoke test and automated prompt-regression pass.
implementation_tasks: Define mosaic schema and data columns (capability tags, econ deltas, latency buckets, compatibility notes).
Build spreadsheet template and Confluence dashboard; include import scripts from benchmark lab outputs.
Assemble 12-model seed list and run baseline prompts across target vertical datasets.
Develop weekly scout digest pipeline: RSS changelog parser + manual field reports ingestion.
Create Solutions hand-off materials: playbook checklist, 2 prompt suites, and negotiation guidance for fallback SLAs.
current_blockers: Benchmark lab needs access to the private dataset for CRM-simulated workloads (request filed with infra). Sales field report ingestion requires a lightweight form; waiting on Growth Ops to approve access. No legal blockers identified yet, but some enterprise customers asked for contract language templates for fallback SLAs.
